title: Don't allocate 1 GB of memory to create a file
body:
`bs=1G` means "read 1GB into memory at a time"; we really don't need that.

On a system with 6GB physical memory (while our test VM is configured to have 8 GB of virtual RAM), this seems to result in trashing and exceeding the 30s timeout, while with a smaller block size, the copy happens in <13 seconds. (`dd` itself reports 11 s vs. 27 s).

comments.body: I don't see why we need such a huge file and why it needs to be filled with random data but the change LGTM

Yes, that is also a question … the test links to an issue saying “a huge context which should be ignored wasn’t”, so the large file seems possibly wanted here. OTOH the test seems to do deterministic checks and does not obviously rely on the file being “too large” / “too slow”.
Maybe that's why someone noticed the effects of not ignoring a big file? For the test itself I don't think we need to reproduce that exactly, it is relatively expensive
